facts.statement: Atopodentatus is an extinct genus of basal sauropterygian.
A near-complete skeleton and part of a skull were found near Daaozi village in Yunnan, China.
facts.quote: A near-complete skeleton along with a left lateral portion of the skull was discovered near Daaozi village, Yunnan, China.

facts.statement: The genus name Atopodentatus comes from the unusual zipper-like shape of the holotype's jaws and teeth.
facts.quote: The scientific name derives from the peculiar zipper-shaped morphology of the holotype specimen's jaws and unique dentition.

facts.statement: The name Atopodentatus means "unusual toothed" in Greek and Latin, referring to the unique tooth arrangement.
facts.quote: The genus name Atopodentatus is derived from the Ancient Greek (άτοπος), meaning "unusual", combined with Latin dentatus, "toothed", referring to the unusual arrangement and shape of the teeth.

facts.statement: Atopodentatus was an herbivorous marine reptile, which is unusual since most marine reptiles are omnivores or carnivores.
facts.quote: Atopodentatus was an herbivorous marine reptile, although marine reptiles are usually omnivores or carnivores.

facts.statement: Atopodentatus was a medium-sized reptile about 2.75 meters long.
facts.quote: Atopodentatus was a medium-sized reptile measuring about 2.75 m long.

facts.statement: Its elongated body, reduced neck, and robust limbs suggest Atopodentatus was likely semi-aquatic.
facts.quote: The geological strata in which the fossil was found, the elongated body, reduced neck, robust appendages and hips of Atopodentatus all suggest that the animal was probably semi-aquatic in nature.

facts.statement: New findings revealed Atopodentatus had a hammer-shaped head with chisel-shaped teeth used for rooting in the seabed.
facts.quote: Discoveries in 2016, however, overthrew these findings, and revealed that Atopodentatus actually had a hammer-shaped head, with a bank of chisel-shaped teeth, that was useful in rooting the seabed for food.

facts.statement: Atopodentatus was a basal marine reptile living in the early Middle Triassic in Luoping, Yunnan, southwestern China.
facts.quote: Atopodentatus es un género extinto de reptil marino, posiblemente un sauropterigio basal, que vivió durante el inicio del Triásico Medio (subetapa del Pelsoniano, etapa del Anisiense) en la región de Luoping en la provincia de Yunnan, en el suroeste de China.

facts.statement: Atopodentatus measured nearly 3 meters in length.
facts.quote: Atopodentatus medía cerca de 3 metros de largo.

facts.statement: The most unusual feature of Atopodentatus was its upper jaw, which had teeth running along the jawline and then vertically in the middle.
facts.quote: La característica más extraña de Atopodentatus es su mandíbula superior, la cual posee dientes que corren a lo largo del borde de la mandíbula y luego quedan en una disposición vertical gracias a una abertura situada en medio de la mandíbula.

facts.statement: Fossils from 2016 indicate the animal actually had a hammer-shaped head with shovel-like jaws.
facts.quote: Sin embargo, dos cráneos fosilizados descubiertos en 2016 indican que el cráneo holotipo estaba muy dañado, y que el animal vivo tendría en realidad una cabeza con apariencia similar a la de un martillo, con mandíbulas amplias que recuerdan a una pala.

facts.statement: Findings from 2016 revealed Atopodentatus ate seabed algae, making it the second known herbivorous marine reptile.
facts.quote: Sin embargo, los hallazgos de 2016 revelaron que Atopodentatus en realidad sería un consumidor de algas del suelo marino, lo cual lo convierte en el segundo reptil marino herbívoro conocido, aparte del esfenodonte Ankylosphenodon.

facts.statement: Atopodentatus belongs to the superorder Sauropterygia.
The genus Atopodentatus was described by Cheng et al. in 2014.
The type species of the genus is Atopodentatus unicus.
The parent group of Atopodentatus is Sauropterygia.
The type species for the genus Atopodentatus is Atopodentatus unicus.

rejected.quote: However, two fossil skulls discovered in 2016 indicate that the holotype skull was badly damaged, and that the living animal actually had a hammer-shaped head with shovel-like jaws.
